_metadata.description: Business Email Compromise scenario-specific derived parameters

base_rate_triangulation._citation: One population (US businesses): FBI IC3 complaints set the base rate and the floor. TEF = LEF ÷ susceptibility.

vector_proportions._citation: Derived from FBI IC3 2024, DBIR 2025, Proofpoint Human Factor 2025, Cofense 2026

bec_overall_share._citation: Derived from DBIR 2025 (social engineering ~20% of breaches, BEC ~50% of SE) + FBI IC3 (BEC is #1 by dollar loss)

bec_sector_shares._citation: Derived from FBI IC3 2024, DBIR 2025, NAIC 2025 BEC loss data. Not from IRIS (IRIS does not publish BEC-specific sector breakdown).

bec_revenue_shares._citation: Derived from FBI IC3 2024 + Coalition 2025. BEC targeting scales less steeply with revenue than ransomware — small businesses are also heavily targeted (payroll diversion, invoice fraud).

bec_revenue_prob_gte2._citation: Not available from IRIS for BEC specifically. All null — tool falls back to overall floor.

credential_tempo._citation: FBI IC3 2024 (21,489 BEC complaints, US) with this scenario's own underreporting factor (operational_tempo_note) and credential vector share; US addressable population as in the base rate.
credential_tempo._derivation: campaigns/month = 21,489 × [5, 7.5, 10] ÷ 12 = [8,954, 13,431, 17,908] (US; each BEC event targets one organization); credential_proportion = BEC's credential vector share (account takeover of business email); addressable population = ~6M US businesses (Census), matching IC3's US scope. Replaces earlier judgment values (300-1,500 campaigns/month, 15-35%).
credential_tempo._geography_note: IC3 complaints are US victims over US firms, so the ceiling's geography multiplier is relative to the US (US = 1.0). Ransomware, exfiltration and web app count campaigns worldwide over a global population and keep the absolute multiplier.
credential_tempo.note: BEC credential vector = account takeover via compromised business email. Tempo is lower than ransomware because BEC account compromise campaigns are more targeted.

exploitation_scanning._citation: BEC rarely involves exploitation. Minimal values reflecting edge cases (email server exploits, MFA bypass vulnerabilities).
exploitation_scanning.grn_malicious_rate_note: Shared with ransomware: the GreyNoise IP-level malicious rate describes scanning, not the scenario; the scenario enters through ransomware_proportion_of_scanning and PoA.
exploitation_scanning.grn_suspicious_rate_note: Not meaningful for BEC — exploitation is not a primary BEC vector.
exploitation_scanning.campaign_ip_ratio_note: Copied from ransomware. Rarely binding for BEC.
exploitation_scanning.poa_ransomware_note: For BEC, this is 'probability of email server exploitation leading to BEC' — very low.
exploitation_scanning.ransomware_proportion_note: Minimal. BEC operators almost never scan for exploitable infrastructure.

output_templates.one_sentence: Based on industry data, BEC operators {attempt_verb} organizations matching your profile {recurrence} (range: {low} to {high}).

base_rate_lef._method: Same recipe as ransomware with one tier: US BEC events per year (FBI IC3 complaints × reporting multiplier) ÷ US firms. The revenue multiplier then applies.
base_rate_lef._n_us_note: FBI IC3 2025 report p.7: Business Email Compromise 24,768 complaints ($3,046,598,558 losses, p.8).
base_rate_lef._underreporting_note: Judgment, no data: how many BEC losses never reach IC3. The one assumed input of this base rate.
base_rate_lef._geography_note: The base rate counts US events over US firms, so the geography multiplier is relative to the US (US = 1.0).

floor_lef._citation: FBI IC3 2025 BEC complaints ÷ US firms (24,768 ÷ 6,395,635): reported losses only, so a lower bound.
